A Unified Reference on American Disease Nomenclature, Pneumococcal Serology, and Pathogen Chains
Educational & Virological Reference Manuscript — Systematic Pathogen Mapping
Integrating historical American vernacular disease names with Latin taxonomy, virology, vaccinological mechanisms,
This expanded manuscript codifies the complete 53-entry transposition chain bridging historical American vernacular disease names to modern virology, microbiology, and vaccinology:

$$\text{\textbf{American Name}} \longrightarrow \text{\textbf{Latin Disease}} \longrightarrow \text{\textbf{Symptomology}} \longrightarrow \text{\textbf{Bacterial Pathogens}} \longrightarrow \text{\textbf{Fungi / Yeast / Mold}} \longrightarrow \text{\textbf{Immunoglobulins \& Vaccines}} \longrightarrow \text{\textbf{Serotyping / Genotyping}} \longrightarrow \text{\textbf{Viral Endpoint}}$$

Polysaccharide vaccines (PPSV23) induce systemic IgG2 immunoglobulins, whereas protein-conjugated vaccines (PCV13/15/20) recruit T-helper CD4+ cells to induce T-cell dependent IgG1/IgG3 subclass switching, affinity maturation, and mucosal IgA secretory immunity.

Part III: Analytical Synthesis & Vaccinological Integration
Resolution of Gaps through Virology & Vaccinology:

Every historic American entry is mapped to modern pathogen chains. By integrating viral endpoints (e.g., Parainfluenza for Croup, Enteroviruses and Arboviruses for Brain Fever, Rotavirus/Norovirus for Summer Complaint) alongside vaccine immunogens (DTaP, PPSV23, PCV20, MenACWY, RTS,S/AS01, IPV/OPV), the structural ledger is completely resolved.
